{{Short description|French physicist (born 1963)}}
'''Thierry Giamarchi''' (born 1963) is a French [[physicist]].

== Biography ==
Thierry Giamarchi studied in [[Toulouse]] and [[Marseille]] and after preparatory classes at the Lycée Thiers became a student at the [[École normale supérieure (Paris)|École Normale Supérieure]] (1982). He passed his [[thesis]] under the direction of H.J. Schulz at the [[Paris-Sud University]] (now Paris-Saclay) in 1987.

He has been a permanent researcher at the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research|CNRS]] since 1986, and during the period 1990-1992 did a postdoctoral fellowship at [[Bell Labs|Bell Laboratories]] (USA).  In 2002 he became full professor at the [[University of Geneva]] in the Department of Quantum Matter Physics (DQMP) and was head of this department from 2013 to 2019. He is currently vice-president (since 2017) of a Swiss association on materials with remarkable electronic properties (MaNEP<ref>{{cite web |date= |title=MaNEP: Steering Committee 2021-2023 |url=https://manep.ch/executive-board/}}</ref>).

In addition to his research activities, he has been in charge of several administrative activities such as the direction of the Department of Quantum Matter Physics (DQMP)<ref>{{cite web |date= |title=DQMP - People directory alphabetized listing |url=https://dqmp.unige.ch/about-us/directory/}}</ref> (2013-2019), member of the Research Commission of the University of Geneva (2018-2020), member of the CNRS National Committee for Theoretical Physics (2000-2002), member of the Scientific Committee of the School of Physics of [[Les Houches]] (2007-2016) or member of the Scientific Council of the [[Commissariat à l'énergie atomique|Commissariat à l'Énergie Atomique]] (CEA) (2015-2018).

Since 2013, he has been a member of the [[French Academy of Sciences|French Academy of sciences]]<ref>{{cite web |date= |title=Académie des sciences: Thierry Giamarchi |url=https://www.academie-sciences.fr/fr/Liste-des-membres-de-l-Academie-des-sciences-/-G/thierry-giamarchi.html |website=Academie de Sciences Institut de France}}</ref> and a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]].<ref>{{cite web |date= |title=American Physical Society: Thierry Giamarchi |url=https://physics.aps.org/authors/thierry_giamarchi |website=[[American Physical Society]]}}</ref>

== Research ==
His research has focused on the effects of interactions in low-dimensional quantum systems, as well as on the combined effects of disorder and interactions in both classical and quantum systems. This work has led to the discovery of new disordered phases such as Bose glass and Bragg glass.

For quantum systems his work has focused on the effects of interactions in one- or nearly one-dimensional quantum structures, known as Tomonaga-Luttinger liquids.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Giamarchi |first=Thierry |title=Quantum physics in one dimension |date=2004 |publisher=[[Oxford University Press]] |isbn=978-0-19-171190-9 |doi=10.1093/acprof:oso/9780198525004.001.0001}}</ref> In particular, he has studied how such effects can occur in systems such as organic superconductors<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Schwartz |first1=A. |last2=Dressel |first2=M. |last3=Grüner |first3=G. |last4=Vescoli |first4=V. |last5=Degiorgi |first5=L. |last6=Giamarchi |first6=T. |date=1998-07-15 |title=On-chain electrodynamics of metallic (TMTSF)2X salts: Observation of Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid response |journal=[[Physical Review B]] |publisher=[[American Physical Society]] |volume=58 |issue=3 |page=1261 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.58.1261|arxiv=cond-mat/9801198 }}</ref> or coupled quantum spin chains.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Klanjšek |first1=M. |last2=Mayaffre |first2=H. |last3=Berthier |first3=C. |last4=Horvatić |first4=M. |last5=Chiari |first5=B. |last6=Piovesana |first6=O. |last7=Bouillot |first7=P. |last8=Kollath |first8=C. |last9=Orignac |first9=E. |last10=Citro |first10=R. |last11=Giamarchi |first11=T. |date=2008-09-26 |title=Controlling Luttinger Liquid Physics in Spin Ladders under a Magnetic Field |journal=[[Physical Review Letters]] |publisher=[[American Physical Society]] |volume=101 |issue=13 |article-number=137207 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.101.137207|pmid=18851492 |arxiv=0804.2639 |bibcode=2008PhRvL.101m7207K }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Chitra |first1=R. |last2=Giamarchi |first2=T. |date=1997-03-01 |title=Critical properties of gapped spin-chains and ladders in a magnetic field |journal=[[Physical Review B]] |publisher=[[American Physical Society]] |volume=55 |issue=9 |page=5816 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.55.5816|arxiv=cond-mat/9611114 |bibcode=1997PhRvB..55.5816C }}</ref>

He also showed that such systems have properties normally associated with travelling systems, such as Bose-Einstein condensation,<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Giamarchi |first1=T. |last2=Tsvelik |first2=A.M. |date=1999-05-01 |title=Coupled ladders in a magnetic field |journal=[[Physical Review B]] |publisher=[[American Physical Society]] |volume=59 |issue=17 |article-number=11398 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.59.11398|arxiv=cond-mat/9810219 |bibcode=1999PhRvB..5911398G }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Giamarchi |first1=Thierry |last2=Rüegg |first2=Christian |last3=Tchernyshyov |first3=Oleg |date=2008-03-03 |title=Bose–Einstein condensation in magnetic insulators |journal=[[Nature Physics]] |volume=4 |issue=3 |pages=198–204 |doi=10.1038/nphys893|arxiv=0712.2250 |bibcode=2008NatPh...4..198G }}</ref> and thus could be used as quantum simulators for such systems. Tomonaga-Luttinger's liquid physics is relevant not only for condensed matter but also for ultra-cold atom systems.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Cazalilla |first1=M. A. |last2=Citro |first2=R. |last3=Giamarchi |first3=T. |last4=Orignac |first4=E. |last5=Rigol |first5=M. |date=2011-12-01 |title=One dimensional bosons: From condensed matter systems to ultracold gases |journal=[[Reviews of Modern Physics]] |publisher=[[American Physical Society]] |volume=83 |issue=4 |page=1405 |doi=10.1103/RevModPhys.83.1405|arxiv=1101.5337 |bibcode=2011RvMP...83.1405C }}</ref>

In the presence of disorder he studied, in collaboration with H.J. Schulz, the combined effects of disorder and interactions on one-dimensional interacting [[boson]]s or [[fermion]]s and showed that the interactions significantly modified the effects of disorder. Especially for bosons this combination of interactions and disorder leads to a transition between a superfluid and a localized phase of bosons known as Bose glass.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Giamarchi |first1=T. |last2=Schulz |first2=H. J. |date=1988-01-01 |title=Anderson localization and interactions in one-dimensional metals |journal=[[Physical Review B]] |publisher=[[American Physical Society]] |volume=37 |issue=1 |pages=325–340 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.37.325|pmid=9943580 |bibcode=1988PhRvB..37..325G }}</ref> This phase is currently being intensively studied in the context of ultra-cold atoms.

For classical systems he has shown, in collaboration with P. Le Doussal,<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Giamarchi |first1=Thierry |last2=Le Doussal |first2=Pierre |date=1995-07-01 |title=Elastic theory of flux lattices in the presence of weak disorder |journal=[[Physical Review B]] |publisher=[[American Physical Society]] |volume=52 |issue=2 |pages=1242–1270 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.52.1242|pmid=9980705 |arxiv=cond-mat/9501087 |bibcode=1995PhRvB..52.1242G }}</ref> that the effects of disorder on periodic elastic structures, such as the [[Abrikosov vortex]] grating in a superconductor, led to a new vitreous phase of the matter having the appearance of a solid (Bragg glass), a phase that could be revealed by [[neutron diffraction]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Klein |first1=T. |last2=Joumard |first2=I. |last3=Blanchard |first3=S. |last4=Marcus |first4=J. |last5=Cubitt |first5=R. |last6=Giamarchi |first6=T. |last7=Le Doussal |first7=P. |date=2001-09-27 |title=A Bragg glass phase in the vortex lattice of a type II superconductor |journal=Nature |volume=413 |issue=6854 |pages=404–406 |doi=10.1038/35096534|pmid=11574883 |arxiv=cond-mat/0110018 |bibcode=2001Natur.413..404K }}</ref> This work, as well as the study of the dynamics of such systems,<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Giamarchi |first1=T. |last2=Le Doussal |first2=P. |date=1996-04-29 |title=Moving Glass Phase of Driven Lattices |journal=[[Physical Review Letters]] |publisher=[[American Physical Society]] |volume=76 |issue=18 |pages=3408–3411 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.76.3408|pmid=10060959 |arxiv=cond-mat/9512006 |bibcode=1996PhRvL..76.3408G }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Chauve |first1=Pascal |last2=Giamarchi |first2=Thierry |last3=Le Doussal |first3=Pierre |date=2000-09-01 |title=Creep and depinning in disordered media |journal=[[Physical Review B]] |publisher=[[American Physical Society]] |volume=62 |issue=10 |page=6241 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.62.6241|arxiv=cond-mat/0002299 |bibcode=2000PhRvB..62.6241C }}</ref> is also directly relevant to the properties of materials useful for information storage such as magnetic films<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Lemerle |first1=S. |last2=Ferré |first2=J. |last3=Chappert |first3=C. |last4=Mathet |first4=V. |last5=Giamarchi |first5=T. |last6=Le Doussal |first6=P. |date=1998-01-26 |title=Domain Wall Creep in an Ising Ultrathin Magnetic Film |journal=[[Physical Review Letters]] |publisher=[[American Physical Society]] |volume=80 |issue=4 |page=849 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.80.849|bibcode=1998PhRvL..80..849L }}</ref> and ferroelectrics.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Tybell |first1=T. |last2=Paruch |first2=P. |last3=Giamarchi |first3=T. |last4=Triscone |first4=J.M. |date=2002-08-09 |title=Domain Wall Creep in Epitaxial Ferroelectric Pb(Zr0.2Ti0.8)O3 Thin Films |journal=[[Physical Review Letters]] |publisher=[[American Physical Society]] |volume=89 |issue=9 |article-number=097601 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.89.097601|pmid=12190438 |arxiv=cond-mat/0203381 }}</ref>

== Awards ==
* 2000: Abragam prize of the French Academy of sciences
* 2013: Member of the French Academy of sciences
* 2013: Fellow of the American Physical Society
